skills.name: okr-intake
skills.description: Use when onboarding an org's orphan packages into OKRs — interview, long-form run, ~12 plan decisions, a guesses brief.
skills.when_to_use: The standing ONBOARDING lane every repo/org goes through once, and re-runs cheaply forever after. FOUR PHASES: (1) a CSE-style upfront interview that SEEDS classification — multiple choice plus clarification, asked dynamically, and PERSISTED so every re-run starts better; (2) a long-form, walk-away-able engine run (quarantine → corpus → free organize_area seeding → match → cluster → plan → lint → self-check) that never throws and degrades honestly; (3) a PLAN-LEVEL approval conversation of ~12 decisions, ceiling 20, NEVER per row — one decision fans out to every member link, because a 970-item review queue is an ignored backlog by construction; (4) a completion brief with an explicit 'places I guessed on your behalf' section. This is the PACKAGE lane — the only OKR skill that reaches the ~970 orphan packages. Auto-apply is OFF by default: the pass runs dry first, shows what WOULD be written, and only then offers the lever. It NEVER creates objectives or key results — humans accept on /objectives. Triggers on 'okr intake', 'onboard this repo into OKRs', 'what work is not laddering to an objective', 'classify our orphan packages', 'reconcile the alignment score'.

skills.name: okr-seams
skills.description: Use when you want seam OKRs — develop a seam, run persona auto/confirm passes, discuss a big goal, or roundup into org objectives.
skills.when_to_use: Seam-OKR development loop over the architecture topics. OPENER: a seam-pressure ranking table (liveness × drift × scaling severity) over EVERY topic — ranking orders attention, never excludes. DEVELOP (default): walk ONE seam — machine maturity numbers, the if-we-scaled outlook, open steering-queue drafts, live seam OKRs — refine conversationally, then promote through the steering-queue accept path (promoteSeamDraft) into a live level='seam' objective. The strategic companion may be read live as privileged interview context but its text is NEVER persisted anywhere. ROUNDUP: cluster all live seam objectives across topics, run the upstream-assignment Q&A per cluster (existing org objectives + 'Create new'), and queue kind='seam_upstream' drafts (writeUpstreamProposals); missing-upstream findings are explicit output. STRATEGY-LOOP MODES: AUTO — a charter-seeded persona develops EVERY seam into the steering queue (nothing promoted; accept path stays human-only). CONFIRM — same, plus one confirm question per seam. GOAL — gap-analyze a stated near-term goal against live objectives/seams → horizon-tagged drafts + seam re-eval flags. CONSOLIDATE — end-of-pass clustering of open findings into OKR-mapped spec-bundle PROPOSALS (priority score + runtime estimate); each APPROVED cluster becomes one DRAFT package — nothing live, nothing launched. All modes capture misalignments as draft finding packages. Triggers on 'seam okrs', 'develop okrs for <topic>', 'okr roundup', 'component okrs', 'seam pressure', 'okr auto pass', 'okr goal <text>'.

skills.name: onboard-charter
skills.description: Charter-first onboarding — the interview that creates the org's ONE intent store. Successor to /cse:onboard-goals; fixes CHARTER_MISSING.
skills.when_to_use: The FIRST OKR-lane conversation for any org/repo, and the remedy every charter-dependent engine names: lattice drafting and archaeology v2 refuse to run without a saved charter (requireCharter throws CHARTER_MISSING pointing here). Three movements: (1) machine recon — `node bin/cascade.js charter-onboard --recon` detects the repo's surfaces (web, electron, cli-plugin, daemon, native, substrate, menu-bar) with evidence, and emits 5-10 deterministic strategy hypotheses phrased for cheap confirm/deny; (2) a HUMAN interview — hypotheses confirmed/denied/revised, then mission, near/long horizon goals, non-goals, per-surface intent, trade-offs, cadence, day zero, all via AskUserQuestion, one stage at a time; (3) an apply-gated write — saveCharter (versioned artifact, one node per org) plus organizations.okr_cadence/okr_day_zero. Dry-run by default; NOTHING is written without an explicit apply. Triggers on 'onboard charter', 'set up the charter', 'charter interview', 'what is this org actually trying to do', 'CHARTER_MISSING', and as the handoff before OKR lattice drafting.

skills.name: onboard-goals
skills.description: Short goals interview writing the goal frame triage classifies against. Creates no OKRs. SUPERSEDED by /cse:onboard-charter.
skills.when_to_use: SUPERSEDED — the charter absorbs the goal frame, so run /cse:onboard-charter instead for new orgs; this remains only for orgs already on a goal frame. The goals interview that runs BEFORE any import or triage pass. A short conversational interview (5-8 questions, one at a time, options drawn from what is already in the org) that extracts named THEMES with matchable keywords, rough TIME PERIODS that matter, the SYSTEMS whose history is worth keeping, and KNOWN DEAD ENDS the user already considers abandoned — then persists them as a new VERSION of the org's goal frame via cascade-web/src/lib/triage/goalFrame.ts. Theme ids are STABLE across re-runs because triage_classifications.theme_ids references them. This skill NEVER creates objectives or key results — OKRs are framed deliberately forward with real buy-in; this only makes laddering history backward onto them cheap. Triggers on 'onboard goals', 'set up the goal frame', 'what are we trying to do', 'before we import, tell Cascade the goals', 'add a theme to the goal frame'.
